precepts.text: The eye of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying no eye shall see me, and disguiseth his face. The white man who rapes, robs, and pillages disguises his face as the Jews, as Jesus, as the angels, and nobody believes he did all this.
precepts.point: In 1948 they got the land again, set up schools, and taught a new Hebrew. Biblical Hebrew was extinct from 70 AD; the father of modern Hebrew fused French, Arabic, Aramaic, Spanish, and German words, and now Negroes argue over it. They got the land, made a language, called themselves Jewish, and the prophecy says they shall fall.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
This one is rarely read, but it says the same thing as Job 9:24. “The eye also of the adulterer”: that is this white man; he is the adulterer. He rapes and robs and pillages women. That's what they do.

“waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.” He disguises his face as the Jews. He disguises his face as Jesus. He disguises his face as the angels. And everybody goes, no, nobody could believe that this man did all this.

So the robbers of thy people in Daniel 11:14 establish the vision in disguise. They exalt themselves as the Jews wearing a face that is not theirs, thinking no eye shall see them, and that is why the world cannot believe what they have done.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not remove thy neighbor's landmark which they of old time have set in thine inheritance.
precepts.point: They drive away the ass of the fatherless and take the widow's ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way, and the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job says, “Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof.” The law forbids it: “Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour’s landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance, which thou shalt inherit in the land that the Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it.”

The landmark was set of old time in the inheritance the Lord gave. Removing it is the wicked moving into your land and naming it after themselves. That is the crime of the oppressor Job is describing, and times are not hidden from the Almighty.

precepts.text: His soul lifted up is not upright; he transgresseth by wine, enlargeth his desire as hell, and gathereth unto him all nations and all people; that is America.
precepts.point: They drive away the ass of the fatherless and take the widow's ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way, and the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.” The one who removes the landmarks and takes the flocks is described here: “because he transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home, who enlargeth his desire as hell, and is as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people”.

That is America. A proud man who does not keep at home, whose desire is enlarged as hell and cannot be satisfied, gathering all nations and heaping all people to himself. That is who violently takes away flocks and feeds thereof, drives away the ass of the fatherless and turns the needy out of the way. His soul lifted up is not upright; the just live by faith.

precepts.text: Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house.
precepts.point: They drive away the ass of the fatherless and take the widow's ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way, and the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why: “Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evil!” The one who removes the landmarks and takes the flocks and the widow's ox does it out of an evil covetousness, to set his nest on high. Woe is pronounced on him. Times are not hidden from the Almighty, and the oppressor's day is coming.

precepts.text: They covet fields and take them by violence, and houses and take them away; they oppress a man, his house, his heritage, changing your name.
precepts.point: They drive away the ass of the fatherless and take the widow's ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way, and the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.” That is Job's “they violently take away flocks” in Micah's words: coveting fields and taking them by violence, taking houses away, oppressing a man, his house and his heritage.

Taking a man's heritage is changing your name. They move into your land, name it after themselves and take away who you are. That is what removing the landmarks comes to.

precepts.text: A nation swift as the eagle, of fierce countenance, whose symbol is the eagle, shall eat the fruit of your cattle and land until you are destroyed.
precepts.point: They drive away the ass of the fatherless and take the widow's ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way, and the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
The oppressor Job describes was foretold in the curses: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. A nation swift as the eagle, whose symbol is the eagle.

“And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed: which also shall not leave thee either corn, wine, or oil, or the increase of thy kine, or flocks of thy sheep, until he have destroyed thee.” That is the one who violently takes away flocks and feeds thereof, takes the widow's ox for a pledge and turns the needy out of the way: eating the fruit of our cattle and our land until we are destroyed.

precepts.text: Thy sons and daughters given to another people, and thine eyes shall look and fail with longing for them all day long.
precepts.point: They which make oil within their walls and tread their winepresses still suffer thirst. This is the curse where you plant vineyards and do not eat from them, left neither corn nor wine.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.” That is a curse on us: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.”

The fatherless plucked from the breast are our sons and daughters given to another people, while our eyes look and fail with longing for them all the day long and there is no might in our hand to stop it. The oppressor's crime is the curse we were told would come.

precepts.text: Mine eyes run down with water, because the comforter that should relieve my soul is far from me.
precepts.point: They which make oil within their walls and tread their winepresses still suffer thirst. This is the curse where you plant vineyards and do not eat from them, left neither corn nor wine.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Our children given to another people brings this weeping: “For these things I weep; mine eye, mine eye runneth down with water, because the comforter that should relieve my soul is far from me: my children are desolate, because the enemy prevailed.”

The children are desolate because the enemy prevailed, plucked from the breast as Job says, and the comforter that should relieve the soul is far away. Those who make oil within their walls and tread their winepresses still suffer thirst: that is the curse where you plant vineyards and do not eat from them, left neither corn nor wine.

precepts.text: Whose possessors slay them and hold themselves not guilty; your last name shows who owns you, that is the real name brand.
precepts.point: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof nor abide in the paths thereof. The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief. He will kill you in broad daylight.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out”. Zechariah tells who they are: “Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not.”

We have possessors. Your last name shows who owns you; that is the real name brand. Those possessors slay us and hold themselves not guilty, and those who sold us said blessed be the Lord, for I am rich. That is “The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy”: he will kill you in broad daylight and count himself not guilty.

precepts.text: Thus saith the Lord my God, feed the flock of the slaughter; we are the ones being killed with no assurance of life.
precepts.point: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof nor abide in the paths thereof. The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief. He will kill you in broad daylight.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why: “Thus saith the Lord my God; Feed the flock of the slaughter”. We are the flock of the slaughter, the ones being killed with no assurance of life. The wounded whose soul cries out from the city, the poor and needy the murderer kills rising with the light, that is the flock of the slaughter, and the word from the Lord is to feed it.

precepts.text: In the morning you shall say, would God it were even, and at evening, would God it were morning; you cannot tell if day or night is worse.
precepts.point: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof nor abide in the paths thereof. The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief. He will kill you in broad daylight.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.” Day or night there is no safety, which is the curse: “In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning! for the fear of thine heart wherewith thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.”

You cannot tell if day or night is worse. The murderer kills in broad daylight and comes as a thief by night, so the fear of the heart and the sight of the eyes never let up.

precepts.point: They scope you out in the daytime, marking your house, then come back at nighttime to hit you. For the morning is to them as the shadow of death; if one knows them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job says, “The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.” Ecclesiasticus describes that same man: “All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die. A man that breaketh wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins”.

“Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.” The adulterer, and those who scope you out in the daytime, mark your house and come back at night to dig through it, know not the light; they only fear the eyes of men. But the Lord beholds all the ways of men and considers the most secret parts. That is why the morning is to them as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.

precepts.text: They shall look upon the carcasses of the men that transgressed; their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched.
precepts.point: The womb shall forget him, the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered, and wickedness shall be broken as a tree. He evil entreateth the barren that beareth not and doeth not good to the widow.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered”. Isaiah shows the end of those who have sinned: “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.”

The worm feeds sweetly on the wicked, and their worm shall not die. As drought and heat consume the snow waters, so the grave consumes those which have sinned, and wickedness is broken as a tree. Their portion is cursed in the earth, and they are an abhorring unto all flesh.

precepts.text: Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee, and thou shalt fear day and night, and have none assurance of thy life.
precepts.point: And if it be not so now, who will make Job a liar and make his speech nothing worth? The prophecy will come true because Job is speaking as the mouthpiece of God.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job says “he riseth up, and no man is sure of life.” That is the curse: “And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”.

No assurance of life, failing eyes and sorrow of mind. The mighty one draws with his power and rises up, and under him our life hangs in doubt and we fear day and night. Job is describing the curse we live under.

precepts.text: Shall the unbelief of some make the faith of God without effect? God forbid; let God be true, but every man a liar, that Job be justified in his sayings.
precepts.point: And if it be not so now, who will make Job a liar and make his speech nothing worth? The prophecy will come true because Job is speaking as the mouthpiece of God.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job ends, “And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?” Paul answers: “For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.”

Job is speaking as the mouthpiece of God, so the prophecy will come true. The unbelief of some cannot make the faith of God without effect. Let God be true and every man a liar, that Job be justified in his sayings: the wicked are exalted for a little while, then gone and brought low, taken out of the way and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.

precepts.text: Drought and heat consume the snow waters; so does the grave those which have sinned. The grave is what waits for those who commit sin, and that is what David is referring to.
precepts.point: When the Most High rebukes a man for iniquity, he makes his beauty consume away like a moth. When man commits iniquity the Lord corrects, and many times people end up dying when they commit iniquity.

note.label: Psalm 39: David Mourns His Frailty and Prays to Recover Strength

precepts.why:
“When thou with rebukes dost correct man for iniquity, thou makest his beauty to consume away like a moth”. Job shows what that consuming is: “Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned.” The grave is what waits for those who commit sin, and that is what David is referring to. When man commits iniquity the Lord corrects, and many times people end up dying when they commit iniquity.

This is what we must keep in mind as we walk: there is really one thing waiting for us if we are not keeping the commandments, and that is the grave. For some who keep the commandments the grave may still come, but eternal life waits after it. David understood this, which is why he repented.
